title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 23. The Pastimes of Sri Nityananda
html:
Nityananda with Shachi: she sees Rama and Krishna eating her food; Nityananda's appearance; robbers become devotees; Krishnadasa of Badagachhi; Nityananda fills the world with the name of Krishna Chaitanya

Verse 1

तत आगत्य प्रथमं श्रीशचीदर्शनोत्सुकः।
प्रणम्य चरणोपान्ते मातरागतोऽहं सुखम्॥१॥

tata āgatya prathamaṁ śrīśacīdarśanotsukaḥ|
praṇamya caraṇopānte mātarāgato'haṁ sukham||1||

tatah — then; agatya — having come; prathamam — first of all; shri-shachi-darshana-utsukah — eager to see Sri Shachi; pranamya — bowing; charana-upante — at her feet; matah — Mother; agatah — have come; aham — I; sukham — happily.

1Coming then to Navadvipa, eager above all to see Sri Shachi, He bowed at her feet and said, "Mother, I have come, and I am happy!"

Verse 2

श्रुत्वा सा सत्वरं माता तस्य मूर्ध्नि करद्वयम्।
धृत्वा तातेति सम्बोध्य संचुम्ब्य च मुहुर्मुहुः॥२॥

śrutvā sā satvaraṁ mātā tasya mūrdhni karadvayam|
dhṛtvā tāteti sambodhya saṁcumbya ca muhurmuhuḥ||2||

shrutva — hearing; sa — she; satvaram — at once; mata — the mother; tasya — His; murdhni — on the head; kara-dvayam — both hands; dhritva — placing; tata — child; iti — thus; sambodhya — addressing; samchumbya — kissing; cha — and; muhuh muhuh — again and again.

2Hearing this, the mother at once placed both her hands on His head, called Him "my child," and kissed Him again and again.

Verse 3

उवाच मधुरं तात स्थातुमर्हसि मद्गृहे।
येन त्वां सर्वदा तात पश्यामि दुःखच्छेदकम्॥३॥

uvāca madhuraṁ tāta sthātumarhasi madgṛhe|
yena tvāṁ sarvadā tāta paśyāmi duḥkhacchedakam||3||

uvacha — said; madhuram — sweetly; tata — child; sthatum arhasi — please stay; mat-grihe — in my house; yena — so that; tvam — You; sarvada — always; tata — child; pashyami — I may see; duhkha-chchhedakam — who cuts away sorrow.

3She said sweetly, "Child, stay in my house, so that I may always see You — You who cut away sorrow."

Verse 4

प्रहसन् प्राह तां मातः शृणु सत्यं वदामि ते।
वसामि सानुजोऽहं ते सदा सन्निहितोऽपि च॥४॥

prahasan prāha tāṁ mātaḥ śṛṇu satyaṁ vadāmi te|
vasāmi sānujo'haṁ te sadā sannihito'pi ca||4||

prahasan — laughing; praha — said; tam — to her; matah — Mother; shrinu — listen; satyam — the truth; vadami — I tell; te — you; vasami — I dwell; sa-anujah — with My younger brother; aham — I; te — near you; sada — always; sannihitah — close at hand; api cha — and.

4Laughing, He replied to her, "Mother, listen, I will tell you the truth: I and My younger brother1 always live beside you, always close to you.

Verse 5

त्वया पाचितमन्नं यत् श्रीकृष्णाधरपूरितम्।
तल्लोभेन सदा मातस्तिष्ठामि तव सन्निधौ॥५॥

tvayā pācitamannaṁ yat śrīkṛṣṇādharapūritam|
tallobhena sadā mātastiṣṭhāmi tava sannidhau||5||

tvaya — by you; pachitam — cooked; annam — food; yat — which; shri-krishna-adhara-puritam — filled with (the nectar of) Sri Krishna's lips; tat-lobhena — out of longing for it; sada — always; matah — Mother; tishthami — I stay; tava sannidhau — near you.

5The food you cook is filled with the nectar of Sri Krishna's lips2 — it is out of longing for it, Mother, that I always stay near you."

Verse 6

एवं श्रुत्वा हसन्ती सा पक्वशाल्यन्नमुत्तमम्।
सूपं तं पायसाद्यं च तमन्नं परमाद्भुतम्॥६॥

evaṁ śrutvā hasantī sā pakvaśālyannamuttamam|
sūpaṁ taṁ pāyasādyaṁ ca tamannaṁ paramādbhutam||6||

evam — thus; shrutva — hearing; hasanti — laughing; sa — she; pakva-shali-annam — cooked shali rice; uttamam — excellent; supam — soup (dal); tam — that; payasa-adyam — sweet rice and the rest; cha — and; tam annam — that food; parama-adbhutam — most wonderful.

6Hearing this, she laughed; and excellent cooked shali rice, dal, sweet rice and other dishes — all that wonderful food —

Verse 7

तस्मै सर्वं विनिवेद्य पश्यन्ती मुखपङ्कजम्।
बुभुजे सानुजः सोऽपि प्रहसन् भक्तवत्सलः॥७॥

tasmai sarvaṁ vinivedya paśyantī mukhapaṅkajam|
bubhuje sānujaḥ so'pi prahasan bhaktavatsalaḥ||7||

tasmai — to Him; sarvam — everything; vinivedya — offering; pashyanti — gazing; mukha-pankajam — at the lotus face; bubhuje — ate; sa-anujah — with His younger brother; sah — He; api — and; prahasan — laughing; bhakta-vatsalah — loving to His devotees.

7she offered to Him, gazing at His lotus face. And He who loves His devotees began to eat, laughing, together with His younger brother.

Verse 8

दृष्ट्वा सा रामकृष्णौ च भुक्तवन्तौ सुखार्णवे।
मग्ना बभूव तां दृष्ट्वा नित्यानन्ददयानिधिः॥८॥

dṛṣṭvā sā rāmakṛṣṇau ca bhuktavantau sukhārṇave|
magnā babhūva tāṁ dṛṣṭvā nityānandadayānidhiḥ||8||

drishtva — seeing; sa — she; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; cha — and; bhuktavantau — eating; sukha-arnave — in an ocean of joy; magna babhuva — was immersed; tam — her; drishtva — seeing; nityananda-daya-nidhih — Nityananda, the treasury of mercy.

8Seeing Rama and Krishna eating, she was plunged in an ocean of joy. Seeing her thus, Nityananda, the treasury of mercy,

Verse 9

प्राह मातः सत्यमेव वचः किं मे वदाधुना।
सा प्राह तात ते सत्यमीश्वरस्य वचो यथा॥९॥

prāha mātaḥ satyameva vacaḥ kiṁ me vadādhunā|
sā prāha tāta te satyamīśvarasya vaco yathā||9||

praha — said; matah — Mother; satyam eva — true indeed; vachah — words; kim — whether; me — My; vada — tell; adhuna — now; sa — she; praha — said; tata — child; te — Your; satyam — true; ishvarasya — of the Lord; vachah — the words; yatha — like.

9said, "Mother, tell Me now: are My words true?" She replied, "Child, Your words are true, like the word of the Lord Himself.

Verse 10

तथापि सानुजं त्वां हि द्रष्टुमिच्छामि सर्वदा।
यथाज्ञा ते सुखं मातः कर्तव्यं मे निरन्तरम्॥१०॥

tathāpi sānujaṁ tvāṁ hi draṣṭumicchāmi sarvadā|
yathājñā te sukhaṁ mātaḥ kartavyaṁ me nirantaram||10||

tatha api — and yet; sa-anujam — with Your younger brother; tvam — You; hi — indeed; drashtum — to see; ichchhami — I wish; sarvada — always; yatha — as; ajna — the command; te — your; sukham — (your) happiness; matah — Mother; kartavyam — is to be done; me — by Me; nirantaram — unceasingly.

10And yet I wish always to see You together with Your younger brother." — "As you command, Mother: it is My task unceasingly to bring you joy."

Verse 11

एवं तत्र स्थितो नित्यानन्दः सर्वसुखप्रदः।
जनयन् परमानन्दं नवद्वीपनिवासिनाम्॥११॥

evaṁ tatra sthito nityānandaḥ sarvasukhapradaḥ|
janayan paramānandaṁ navadvīpanivāsinām||11||

evam — thus; tatra — there; sthitah — staying; nityanandah — Nityananda; sarva-sukha-pradah — the giver of every joy; janayan — producing; parama-anandam — supreme bliss; navadvipa-nivasinam — in the residents of Navadvipa.

11Thus, staying there, Nityananda, the giver of every joy, brought supreme bliss to the residents of Navadvipa;

Verse 12

कुर्वन् सर्वजनान् कृष्णचैतन्यरसभावितान्।
गौराङ्गकीर्तनानन्दो ननर्त स्वजनैः सह॥१२॥

kurvan sarvajanān kṛṣṇacaitanyarasabhāvitān|
gaurāṅgakīrtanānando nanarta svajanaiḥ saha||12||

kurvan — making; sarva-janan — all people; krishnachaitanya-rasa-bhavitan — imbued with the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya; gauranga-kirtana-anandah — blissful in Gauranga's kirtana; nanarta — danced; sva-janaih saha — with His own people.

12He made all people imbued with the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya, and, blissful in Gauranga's kirtana, He danced with His own people.

Verse 13

गन्धचन्दनलिप्ताङ्गो नीलाम्बरसमावृतः।
स्वर्णरौप्यप्रवालाद्यैरलङ्कारैश्च मण्डितः॥१३॥

gandhacandanaliptāṅgo nīlāmbarasamāvṛtaḥ|
svarṇaraupyapravālādyairalaṅkāraiśca maṇḍitaḥ||13||

gandha-chandana-lipta-angah — His body anointed with scents and sandal; nila-ambara-samavritah — clad in blue garments; svarna-raupya-pravala-adyaih — of gold, silver, coral and the like; alankaraih — with ornaments; cha — and; manditah — adorned.

13His body was anointed with scents and sandal; He was clad in blue garments and adorned with ornaments of gold, silver, coral and the like;

Verse 14

कर्पूरताम्बूलाद्यैश्च पूर्णश्रीमुखपङ्कजः।
लौहदण्डधरो रौप्यहारकौस्तुभभूषणः॥१४॥

karpūratāmbūlādyaiśca pūrṇaśrīmukhapaṅkajaḥ|
lauhadaṇḍadharo raupyahārakaustubhabhūṣaṇaḥ||14||

karpura-tambula-adyaih — with camphor, betel and the like; cha — and; purna-shri-mukha-pankajah — whose beautiful lotus mouth was filled; lauha-danda-dharah — holding an iron staff; raupya-hara-kaustubha-bhushanah — adorned with a silver necklace and the Kaustubha.

14His beautiful lotus mouth was filled with camphor, betel and other spices; He held an iron staff and was adorned with a silver necklace and the Kaustubha3;

Verse 15

कुण्डलैकधरः श्रीमान् वनमालाविभूषितः।
वेणुपाणिः सदा कुर्वन् गौराङ्गगुणकीर्तनम्॥१५॥

kuṇḍalaikadharaḥ śrīmān vanamālāvibhūṣitaḥ|
veṇupāṇiḥ sadā kurvan gaurāṅgaguṇakīrtanam||15||

kundala-eka-dharah — wearing a single earring; shriman — beautiful; vana-mala-vibhushitah — adorned with a forest garland; venu-panih — flute in hand; sada — always; kurvan — performing; gauranga-guna-kirtanam — the singing of Gauranga's qualities.

15beautiful, wearing a single earring4, adorned with a forest garland, flute in hand, He ceaselessly sang Gauranga's qualities.

Verse 16

चौरदस्युगणाः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तस्य विभूषणम्।
हर्तुं कुर्वन्ति ते नाना स्वयत्नमाततायिनः॥१६॥

cauradasyugaṇāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tasya vibhūṣaṇam|
hartuṁ kurvanti te nānā svayatnamātatāyinaḥ||16||

chaura-dasyu-ganah — the gangs of thieves and robbers; sarve — all; drishtva — seeing; tasya — His; vibhushanam — ornaments; hartum — to steal; kurvanti — make; te — they; nana — various; sva-yatnam — their efforts; atatayinah — the villains.

16Gangs of thieves and robbers, seeing His ornaments, made every effort to steal them — the villains!

Verse 17

तानेव कृपया पूर्णो नित्यानन्दो महाप्रभुः।
गौराङ्गकीर्तनानन्दपरिपूर्णान् चकार ह॥१७॥

tāneva kṛpayā pūrṇo nityānando mahāprabhuḥ|
gaurāṅgakīrtanānandaparipūrṇān cakāra ha||17||

tan eva — those very ones; kripaya — with mercy; purnah — full; nityanandah — Nityananda; maha-prabhuh — the great Prabhu; gauranga-kirtana-ananda-paripurnan — filled with the bliss of Gauranga's kirtana; chakara ha — made.

17But the great Prabhu Nityananda, full of mercy, made those very men full of the bliss of Gauranga's kirtana.

Verse 18

एवं स विहरन् कृष्णचैतन्यरसभावुकः।
करोति विविधां क्रीडां गोपालबाललीलया॥१८॥

evaṁ sa viharan kṛṣṇacaitanyarasabhāvukaḥ|
karoti vividhāṁ krīḍāṁ gopālabālalīlayā||18||

evam — thus; sah — He; viharan — sporting; krishnachaitanya-rasa-bhavukah — rapt in the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya; karoti — performs; vividham — various; kridam — pastimes; gopala-bala-lilaya — in the play of a cowherd boy.

18Thus sporting, rapt in the rasa of Krishna Chaitanya, He performs all kinds of pastimes in the play of a cowherd boy.

Verse 19

गङ्गातीरं समासाद्य स्वभक्तानां गृहे प्रभुः।
विहरन् स्नेहसम्पूर्णः कृष्णदासगृहं ययौ॥१९॥

gaṅgātīraṁ samāsādya svabhaktānāṁ gṛhe prabhuḥ|
viharan snehasampūrṇaḥ kṛṣṇadāsagṛhaṁ yayau||19||

ganga-tiram — the bank of the Ganga; samasadya — reaching; sva-bhaktanam — of His devotees; grihe — in the houses; prabhuh — the Prabhu; viharan — sporting; sneha-sampurnah — full of affection; krishnadasa-griham — to the house of Krishnadasa; yayau — came.

19Coming to the bank of the Ganga and sporting in the houses of His devotees, the Prabhu, full of affection, came to the house of Krishnadasa.

Verse 20

बडगाछीनिवासी स प्राप्य दुष्प्राप्यमीश्वरम्।
आनन्देनाकुलो भूत्वा धुन्वन् वासो ननर्त ह॥२०॥

baḍagāchīnivāsī sa prāpya duṣprāpyamīśvaram|
ānandenākulo bhūtvā dhunvan vāso nanarta ha||20||

badagachhi-nivasi — the resident of Badagachhi; sah — he; prapya — attaining; dushprapyam — the unattainable; ishvaram — Lord; anandena — with bliss; akulah — beside himself; bhutva — becoming; dhunvan — waving; vasah — his cloth; nanarta ha — danced.

20He, a resident of Badagachhi5, having attained the unattainable Lord, was beside himself with bliss and danced, waving his cloth.

Verse 21

महापुण्यतमो ग्रामो बडगाछीतिसंज्ञकः।
नित्यानन्दस्वरूपस्य विहारो भावि यत्र वै॥२१॥

mahāpuṇyatamo grāmo baḍagāchītisaṁjñakaḥ|
nityānandasvarūpasya vihāro bhāvi yatra vai||21||

maha-punya-tamah — most holy; gramah — the village; badagachhi-iti-samjnakah — called Badagachhi; nityananda-svarupasya — of Nityananda-svarupa; viharah — the pastimes; bhavi — destined to be; yatra — where; vai — indeed.

21The village called Badagachhi is most holy: there the pastimes of Nityananda-svarupa were destined to unfold.

Verse 22

कृष्णदासेन सार्धं श्रीनवद्वीपं समागतः।
विहरन् कीर्तनानन्दो रामदासादिभिर्वृतः॥२२॥

kṛṣṇadāsena sārdhaṁ śrīnavadvīpaṁ samāgataḥ|
viharan kīrtanānando rāmadāsādibhirvṛtaḥ||22||

krishnadasena sardham — together with Krishnadasa; shri-navadvipam — to Sri Navadvipa; samagatah — came; viharan — sporting; kirtana-anandah — blissful in kirtana; ramadasa-adibhih — by Ramadasa and others; vritah — surrounded.

22Together with Krishnadasa, surrounded by Ramadasa6 and others, sporting and blissful in kirtana, He came back to Sri Navadvipa.

Verse 23

श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यनाम्ना परिपूर्णं जगत्त्रयम्।
कृत्वा रराज गोपालैः समं नन्दव्रजे यथा॥२३॥

śrīkṛṣṇacaitanyanāmnā paripūrṇaṁ jagattrayam|
kṛtvā rarāja gopālaiḥ samaṁ nandavraje yathā||23||

shri-krishnachaitanya-namna — with the name of Sri Krishna Chaitanya; paripurnam — filled; jagat-trayam — the three worlds; kritva — making; raraja — shone; gopalaih samam — together with the cowherd boys; nanda-vraje — in Nanda's Vraja; yatha — as.

23Having filled the three worlds with the name of Sri Krishna Chaitanya, He shone with His cowherd boys as once in Nanda's Vraja —

Verse 24

वेत्रवंशीशृङ्गवेणुगुञ्जामालाविभूषितैः।
पार्षदैरावृतः कृष्णकीर्तनामृतवर्षकैः॥२४॥

vetravaṁśīśṛṅgaveṇuguñjāmālāvibhūṣitaiḥ|
pārṣadairāvṛtaḥ kṛṣṇakīrtanāmṛtavarṣakaiḥ||24||

vetra-vamshi-shringa-venu-gunja-mala-vibhushitaih — adorned with staffs, vamshi flutes, horns, venu flutes and gunja garlands; parshadaih — by associates; avritah — surrounded; krishna-kirtana-amrita-varshakaih — who rained the nectar of Krishna's kirtana.

24surrounded by associates adorned with staffs, vamshi flutes, horns, venu flutes and gunja garlands, who rained down the nectar of Krishna's kirtana —

Verse 25

बलदेवः स्वयं गोपो वृन्दारण्यविलासवान्।
तद्रूपं दर्शयन् लोके गौराङ्गप्राणवल्लभः॥२५॥

baladevaḥ svayaṁ gopo vṛndāraṇyavilāsavān|
tadrūpaṁ darśayan loke gaurāṅgaprāṇavallabhaḥ||25||

baladevah — Baladeva; svayam — Himself; gopah — the cowherd; vrindaranya-vilasavan — who sports in Vrindaranya; tat-rupam — that form; darshayan — showing; loke — to the world; gauranga-prana-vallabhah — dear as life to Gauranga.

25Baladeva Himself, the cowherd who sports in Vrindaranya, dear as life to Gauranga, showing the world that very form.

Thus ends the twenty-third sarga, "The Pastimes of Sri Nityananda" (Shri-nityananda-vilasa), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Nityananda is Balarama, and His younger brother is Krishna, who has appeared as Gauranga, the son of Shachi.
  2. That is, the Lord Himself eats what she cooks, and the food becomes His prasada, filled with the nectar of His lips.
  3. The Kaustubha: the jewel on the Lord's chest.
  4. A single earring is a mark of Balarama.
  5. Badagachhi: a village in Bengal; Krishnadasa was a companion of Nityananda who lived there.
  6. Ramadasa: apparently Abhirama (Ramadasa), a companion of Nityananda, Shridama in Krishna's lila (cf. 4.22.11).
